claim: disrobe lifts WebAssembly to structured source that re-parses with every operator lowered, and the execution-eligible functions execute equivalently to the original under wasmtime.
detail: 133 of 133 functions in the 38 PARSEABLE corpus modules are fully op-covered (every operator lowered, output re-parses); 2 corpus modules are skipped on wat-parse/sig-extract failure (malformed corpus source the reference assembler also rejects), so this is 100% of the supported subset, NOT of all wasm; separately, 57 of 57 execution-eligible functions are EXECUTION-EQUIVALENT under wasmtime (original vs recovered: return values, trap parity, linear memory; 6 byte-identical), the remainder op-coverage-only
gate_source: crates/disrobe-pass-wasm-deob/tests/semantic_recovery_corpus.rs measure() = 38 modules parsed / 2 skipped / 133 functions / fully_recovered==133, with the module count and function total pinned by equality and the recovered count floored at 133; tests/semantic_differential.rs = wasmtime execution differential, 57/57 execution-eligible equivalent (6 byte-identical), CI-runnable under --features sandbox; op-coverage is NOT execution-equivalence except for those 57

oracle.external: wasmtime execution differential (original vs recovered: return values, trap parity, linear memory) for the 57 execution-eligible functions; output re-parse for op-coverage
oracle.note: Op-coverage (133/133) means every operator lowered and the output re-parses; it is NOT execution-equivalence. The 57/57 wasmtime figure is the execution-equivalence number and is the stronger of the two. They are distinct and labeled distinctly.

reproduce: cargo test -p disrobe-pass-wasm-deob --test semantic_differential --features sandbox  (op-coverage: cargo test -p disrobe-pass-wasm-deob --test semantic_recovery_corpus)
title: WebAssembly recovery, op-coverage and wasmtime execution differential
